It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of an age that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the ground of human dignity and the motives of the state in this hour? [13, 1075, 1321, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by a culture that treats people as mere “administrative anomalies” or tools for economic growth, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the very moment of your conception? [13, 20, 127, 1143, 1304, 1407, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with a secular world, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by reminding us that we were “bought at a price” [11, 28, 113, 146, 304, 1503, 1515, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, your dignity is not a gift from a “politician” but an inherent quality given by the King of Kings [15, 68, 127, 281, 290, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Blueprint of Dignity (The Image of God)**

**Verse**
“So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them” (Genesis 1:27). [1087, 1129, 1179, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scriptures teach that humanity is the “crowning point of creation,” and the *Imago Dei* defines our “unique relation to God,” setting us “apart from the animals” [1081, 1128, 1313, 1322, Conversation History]. We are God’s “representative and representation” on the earth, possessing “reason... intellect, will, and emotion,” which allows us to enjoy “fellowship with Him and bring glory to His name” [1081, 1128, 1130, Conversation History]. Because “the masterpiece of creation, a human being, was made in God’s image,” our dignity is not earned by “achievement, insights, and wisdom” but is inherent because “the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being” (Genesis 2:7) [301, 327, 1089, 1133, 1406, 1531, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by “worldly philosophies” that measure your worth by a “string of degrees” or your “physical stature,” for “your life is not your own” because you were “bought at a price” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [12, 91, 101, 148, 301, 304, 484, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that you are a “vessel for honor,” fashioned by a “master craftsman” to “bring glory to Christ” [138, 149, 1133, 1238, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, “national greatness” and “beautiful cities” were often seen as “temporal signs” of God’s favor, yet the Jews were warned that “man shall not live by bread alone; but man lives by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD” (Deuteronomy 8:3) [409, 1075, 1137, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, showing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” whose “citizenship is in heaven,” and our ultimate goal is to be “conformed to the image of His Son” (Philippians 3:20; Romans 8:29) [13, 26, 38, 142, 440, 491, 947, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1426, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Heritage of the Womb**

**Verse**
“Behold, children are a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb is a reward” (Psalm 127:3). [898, 905, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “conception is a work of divine providence,” for “God’s always in it when a child is conceived” [130, Conversation History]. Children are not “burdensome” or “accidental,” but are “graciously given” by a “loving, beneficent Father” who “knows your needs” (Genesis 33:5; Matthew 6:32) [3, 4, 31, 898, 1236, Conversation History]. Scripture reveals that “unbelief is the seed” of human cruelty that devalues the young, yet the Lord “heals the brokenhearted” and “gathers the lambs with His arm,” showing that even the smallest life is a “special treasure” (Isaiah 40:11; Exodus 19:5) [1, 123, 771, 774, 985, 1338, 1388, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for the Lord is a “father of the fatherless” who “hears the cry of affliction” (Psalm 68:5; Genesis 16:11) [3, 94, 201, 1161, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” to define the value of a child; instead, “ascribe greatness to our God” by recognizing that “of such is the kingdom of God” (Mark 10:14; Deuteronomy 32:3) [51, 123, 900, 1406, 1503, 1623, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “circumcision” and the “ritual after childbirth” were “shadows” that pointed to the need for “heart holiness” and the removal of “depravity” (Genesis 17:11; Leviticus 12:6) [1163, 1295, 1297, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this, revealing that “true circumcision is that of the heart,” and we find “repose of the soul” not in “ritualized ceremonies” but in “the renewing of your mind” (Romans 2:29; 12:2) [13, 24, 142, 459, 860, 876, 1253, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Prenatal Knowledge and Sovereign Predestination**

**Verse**
“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; before you were born I sanctified you; I ordained you a prophet to the nations” (Jeremiah 1:5). [162, Conversation History]. “Your eyes saw my substance, being yet unformed. And in Your book they all were written, the days fashioned for me, when as yet there were none of them” (Psalm 139:16). [45, 828, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition notes that “foreknowledge” refers to a “predetermination” and “pre-thinking” by God, rather than a mere observation of future events [162, Conversation History]. Before you were “fashioned” as a “work of art” from the “dust of the ground,” God “personally and intimately” planned your existence for His own glory [136, 281, 1133, Conversation History]. This proves that “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” as the Lord “works all things after the counsel of His will,” including the “ordained days” of every person from the moment of conception (Ephesians 1:11; Psalm 139:16) [5, 11, 16, 21, 45, 1132, 1143, 1327, 1408, 1515, 1572, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” knowing that “the Lord knows those who are His” before they draw their first breath (2 Timothy 2:19) [11, 24, 116, 147, 149, 201, 211, 352, 412, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” recognizing that “man shall not live by bread alone” but by the “unfailing Word” of the Creator who “designed and decreed” your very life [13, 24, 101, 130, 1075, 1313, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Legal Personhood**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, the law protected the life of the unborn child, for “compensation was mandatory for accidentally causing a premature birth,” showing that “the fetus was considered a person” (Exodus 21:22) [1249, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “warfare,” teaching that while we “do not war according to the flesh,” we must “contend earnestly” for the “spotless purity of truth” that defends the “least of these” (2 Corinthians 10:4; Jude 3; Matthew 25:40) [11, 13, 21, 32, 91, 92, 101, 1081, 1313, 1316, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Error of Utilitarian Protection (Economic Reasons)**

**Verse**
“ ‘No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be loyal to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon’ ” (Matthew 6:24). [100, 102, 170, 327, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals a “degraded view of human life” in societies where people “trust in their wealth and boast in the multitude of their riches” (Psalm 49:6) [30, 58, 1307, 1532, Conversation History]. When a state protects life only for “economic reasons” or “national greatness,” it is following a “market-driven strategy” that acts as a “spirit of fraud” [20, 104, 409, 1316, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition warns that those who “value tangible and temporal benefits more highly than spiritual blessings” will ultimately be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27) [11, 15, 26, 37, 52, 914, 1061, 1143, 1402, 1720, Conversation History]. True protection of life must arise from the “fear of the LORD,” for “if you love the Lord, you must hate that which is unholy” [6, 119, 120, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “opinion polls” to explain human value, for “one’s life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses” (Luke 12:15) [51, 122, 123, 1341, 1406, 1503, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD” (Proverbs 17:15) [170, 236, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to see that every human being is a “masterpiece” of God, not an “administrative anomaly” to be “registered” for Pharaoh’s tax [113, 1133, 1176, 1233, 1406, 1532, 1709, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 149, 176, 201, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 335, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: “My kingdom is not of this world,” Jesus told Pilate. “If My kingdom were of this world, then My servants would be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jews” (John 18:36). No human kingdom or society can ever merge with God’s kingdom, even partially. Sinful man cannot be a part of the divine reign. That’s why we can never advance God’s kingdom by trying to improve the morals of our society. Good and noble causes may be worthy of support, but they have no impact in helping to usher in the earthly kingdom of Jesus Christ. At best they can only retard the corruption that will always and inevitably characterize human societies and kingdoms.

This principle is the simple dividing line between the gospel of Jesus Christ and every erroneous or demonic belief system. Stripped down to its bare essence, every false religion ever devised by reprobate minds is a merit system. All of them teach that justification is earned or achieved by something the worshiper does for God—some kind of good work, sacrament, or religious ceremony; an act of charity or altruism; an austere lifestyle; or (lately) devotion to some political cause, environmental campaign, or alternative value system. The religious zeal that fallen people cultivate for their chosen cause or credo is never truly self less or sacrificial. The cause becomes a platform from which they look down on others. Most people think exactly like the Pharisee in Jesus’ parable: I’m not as bad as other people; I should be okay. Nothing is more natural to the unregenerate human heart.

As Paul explained to Timothy: The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness.” Now in a large house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also vessels of wood and of earthenware, and some to honor and some to dishonor. Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work. Now flee from youthful lusts and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. (2 Tim. 2:19–22)

Significantly, the adoption of slaves was illustrated, corporately, by the nation of Israel itself. In the Exodus, this nation was liberated from bondage in Egypt and adopted by God. As an expert in the Old Testament, Paul would have readily drawn on passages such as Exodus 4:22, Deuteronomy 14:1–2; 32:5–6; and Hosea 1:10; 11:1—texts that describe the Israelites as God’s adopted children.7 Paul understood that just as “Israel was released from the control of Pharaoh to serve God; the believer was released from the control of sin to serve God. Both are declared by God to be [His] sons.”8 In the same way that Israel was adopted by God (Rom. 9:4), New Testament Christians have been welcomed as children into His family.9

thirteen The Riches of the Paradox While nothing in the Bible is contradictory, many of the Bible’s most provocative and profound truths appear to us paradoxical. Consider, for example, the truth that salvation is both free and costly, or that to be truly rich you must be poor in spirit, or that to find your life you must lose it, or that to be wise you must embrace the foolishness of the gospel.1 Scripture teaches that those who mourn will be comforted; those who give will receive; those who are least will be greatest; those who are humble will be exalted; and those who are last will be first.2 We learn, further, that God uses evil for good; that He is three yet one; and that Jesus Christ, the second member of the Trinity, is simultaneously fully God and fully man.3 These are just some of the wondrous mysteries that the Bible sets forth.
